title: Hormuz shock rewrites Asia’s polyester apparel cost map
summary:
Rising tensions around the Strait of Hormuz are triggering a polyester cost crisis for apparel exporters, as selective tanker access, higher crude prices and freight uncertainty disrupt textile supply chains. 
Sharp rises in PTA, MEG and polyester fibre prices are squeezing margins across India, Bangladesh and Pakistan, leaving mills exposed to higher costs and delayed price revisions from buyers.

title: ICE cotton falls sharply on profit booking, weak US exports
summary:
ICE cotton futures plunged sharply after a steep rally triggered heavy profit booking and long liquidation in an overbought market.
Weak US export sales added pressure, while broader commodity-market losses deepened the decline.
July 2026 cotton fell 3.31 per cent to 83.94 cents per pound, with trading volume surpassing 100,000 contracts amid heightened speculative activity.

title: Seasonally-adjusted US PPI for final demand up 1.4 % in April
summary:
The seasonally-adjusted US producer price index for final demand rose by 1.4 per cent in April—the largest advance since rising by 1.7 per cent in March 2022. 
Prices for final demand goods moved up by 2 per cent in April after rising by 1.9 per cent in March. 
Over 40 per cent of the April advance in prices for final demand goods can be attributed to a 15.6-per cent rise in the gasoline index.

title: India’s annual WPI inflation rate 8.3% YoY in April
summary:
The annual rate of inflation based on all India wholesale price index (WPI) stood at 8.3 per cent YoY in April, provisional data show. 
The index number and inflation rate for April of manufactured products was 151.6 and 4.62 per cent YoY respectively. 
The YoY WPI inflation rates for textiles, apparel and leather and related products in April were 7.3 per cent, 2.2 per cent and 1.25 per cent respectively.

title: Brunello CEO at GFS 2026: My generation is the last to buy blindly
summary:
At GFS 2026, Brunello Cucinelli CEO Riccardo Stefanelli highlighted the need to protect Ladakh’s Pashmina-producing communities through regenerative practices and youth livelihood support.
He said luxury must now be measured by social return, community care and ethical behaviour.
Stefanelli added that younger consumers value quality, story, fair pay and loyal supplier relationships.

title: Why are garment makers betting big on the Indian state of Odisha?
summary:
Odisha is rapidly emerging as a major textile and apparel manufacturing hub, backed by plug-and-play industrial parks, strong policy support and large investments from companies including Page Industries and Epic Group. 
With over ₹7,000 crore investments and thousands of jobs in the pipeline, the state aims to become the textile capital of eastern India by 2030.

title: Luzon Economic Corridor expands partnership to include 7 more nations
summary:
The US, the Philippines and Japan have announced the expansion of the Luzon Economic Corridor partnership to include Australia, Denmark, France, Italy, South Korea, Sweden and the UK. 
Through coordinated investments in transport infrastructure, energy systems, digital connectivity and advanced manufacturing supply chains, the corridor will transform Luzon into a more prosperous and interconnected region.

title: US T&A imports fall 11.9% by volume in Q1, exports also decline
summary:
United States textile and apparel import volumes declined 11.93 per cent year-on-year during January–March 2026 to 21.65 billion SME, with both apparel and non-apparel textile imports weakening.
Exports also fell 8.93 per cent, led by lower yarn and fabric shipments.
The data reflected continued softness in US textile trade following a broader slowdown seen in 2025.

title: UK real GDP up estimated 0.6% in Q1 2026
summary:
UK real GDP is estimated to increase by 0.6 per cent in Q1 2026, following a revised growth of 0.2 per cent in Q4 2025, according to the Office of National Statistics. 
In output terms, all three sectors contributed to growth in the latest quarter. 
GDP is estimated to have increased by an unrevised 1.4 per cent annually in 2025, following a revised growth of 1 per cent in 2024.

title: India's FY26 GDP growth estimated at 7.5%: SBI
summary:
Despite global headwinds, India has maintained strong growth momentum, an SBI newsletter said. 
Rural consumption remains strong and urban consumption shows a consistent uptick since the last festive season. 
It expects Q4 FY26 real GDP growth of closer to 7.2 per cent and nowcasts FY27 GDP growth rate of 6.6 per cent. 
FY26 GDP growth is likely to be at 7.5 per cent.

title: Vietnam’s flat apparel exports hide the real trade signal
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and apparel sector showed modest export growth in early 2026, but stronger fabric imports, rising FDI and growing US market share signalled deeper sourcing confidence. 
While overall US apparel imports declined, Vietnam continued gaining relevance as global buyers used it as a hedge against tariff uncertainty, supply-chain risk and China’s weakening position in the US market.

title: US' Wolverine Worldwide Q1 EPS rises 60% on brand momentum
summary:

Gross margin stayed flat at 47.6 per cent, while operating margin improved to 7.4 per cent. 
Net earnings increased to $20.2 million, and diluted EPS rose to $0.24. 
The company maintained its FY26 revenue outlook of $1.96-1.98 billion.

summary:

PAT rose 17 per cent to ₹270 crore (~$28.15 million), while Q4 revenue hit ₹1,314 crore (~$137 million).

summary:
Bangladesh is shifting its apparel pitch from low-cost production to verifiable, traceable and compliant sourcing.

US tariff relief helps, yet fibre-origin rules and policy uncertainty complicate sourcing decisions.

summary:

UGG Renew, LWG Gold-rated tanneries and comfort-led innovation support the brand’s circular footwear approach.

summary:
Bangladesh trade body BGMEA and US-based Open Supply Hub have signed an MoU to strengthen apparel sector transparency and digitally presenting factory information on the global supply chain platform.
The two sides will create an integrated digital database platform that will enable buyers to directly access information on the location, product categories and special capabilities of garment units.

summary:
Representatives of two top Bangladesh garment trade bodies recently met PM Tarique Rahman and urged him to ensure uninterrupted power and energy supply, quick release of export receipts from banks, reopening of closed factories and easing of customs regulations.
BKMEA raised concerns about misuse of the bond facility and urged action against violators of bond licences.

title: US’ Under Armour eyes gross margin improvement in FY27
summary:
For FY27, Under Armour expects slight revenue decline and margin improvement. 
The company’s FY26 revenue fell 4 per cent to $5 billion, led by weaker North America sales, lower wholesale revenue, and a sharp footwear decline. 
Gross margin narrowed due to tariffs and cost pressures. 
In Q4, revenue slipped 1 per cent as North America weakened, though international and DTC sales grew.

summary:

A major focus is energy transition of the sector.
